statement: A binary min-heap is a complete binary tree, filled level by level from left to right, in which no parent is larger than either of its children. It is stored in an array: the node at index i has its children at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2 and its parent at (i − 1) / 2.

You are given an array values. Starting from an empty min-heap, insert the values one at a time from left to right. Each insert places the new value in the next free slot at the end of the array, then sifts it up: while it is smaller than its parent, the two swap.
Report the root of the finished heap, values[0] of the heap array, which is always the smallest value inserted.

examples.explanation: The finished heap array is [1, 2, 3, 7, 5, 9, 8]. When 1 was inserted it rose from index 3 past 7 and then past 2 to reach the root.
The finished heap array is [0, 1, 3, 2, 6, 7, 4, 9]. The last value inserted, 0, is the smallest, so it sifts all the way up to the root.
